s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic oral ulceration with granulomatous inflammation
salient_findings: Ulcer with clean base and irregular, elevated margins
Histopathological findings of dense diffuse infiltrate with lymphocytes, histiocytes, and fungal forms
key_facts: 40-year-old man from eastern India
Presented with a nonhealing ulcer on the tongue for 4 months
Lesion started as a small painless mass on the right lateral aspect of the tongue
No history of trauma or tongue bite preceding the lesion
Patient denied consuming tobacco or alcohol regularly
Medical history of well-controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus for 2 years
No systemic complaints
No history of high-risk behavior for HIV
Single well-defined ulcer measuring 2 × 2 cm on the right lateral aspect of tongue
Histopathological examination showed dense diffuse infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and fungal forms
Histiocytes and giant cells contained intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo
Special stains highlighted fungal forms
Fungal culture on Sabouraud dextrose agar was negative
HIV-1 and HIV-2 serologic testing were negative

shortlist.label: Histoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo in histiocytes, consistent with histoplasmosis

shortlist.label: Cryptococcosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of fungal forms and granulomatous inflammation, although fungal culture was negative

shortlist.label: Chromoblastomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic oral ulceration with granulomatous inflammation and presence of fungal forms

shortlist.label: Paracoccidioidomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and presence of fungal forms, although less common in this region

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation, although no other systemic complaints or findings suggestive of sarcoidosis

raw.rationale: The presence of intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo within histiocytes and giant cells, as seen in the histopathological examination, is characteristic of Histoplasmosis, especially in the context of a nonhealing ulcer and the patient's geographical location in eastern India.

rejected.label: Cryptococcosis
rejected.why: Typically presents with more severe systemic symptoms and is more commonly associated with immunocompromised patients, which does not fit the patient's profile.

rejected.label: Chromoblastomycosis
rejected.why: Characterized by the presence of sclerotic bodies in the tissue, which were not mentioned in the histopathological findings.

rejected.label: Paracoccidioidomycosis
rejected.why: Usually presents with a more pronounced inflammatory response and is more common in South America, which does not match the patient's geographical location or clinical presentation.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Typically presents with non-caseating granulomas without fungal elements, which contradicts the histopathological findings of this case.
